name: Hotel Sonam Delek
summary: A long-running budget hotel on Tibet Road, a few minutes on foot from MG Marg. Rooms run from plain standard twins to deluxe rooms with balconies that face the Kangchenjunga range on clear mornings. Good for travellers who want the town centre without the MG Marg price tag.
body: Tibet Road climbs gently off the upper end of MG Marg, and Hotel Sonam Delek sits along it. That location is the main reason we suggest it. You walk to the promenade, the taxi stands and the Lal Bazaar market in minutes, so you save the ₹100–200 a day that people in far-off hotels spend on local taxis. The building faces north-west, and the better rooms have balconies looking across the valley to the snow peaks.

Rooms come in several grades. The cheapest standard twins are small and plain; deluxe and super deluxe rooms are larger and carry the view. Breakfast is often bundled into the online rates. Expect a simple, family-run operation rather than polish. Guests praise the views and helpful front desk; some reviews mention tired fittings and limited breakfast, which is fair for the price band.
why: Walking distance to MG Marg and the taxi stands
View rooms of the Kangchenjunga range in clear weather
Wide spread of room grades suits tight budgets
watch_out: The cheapest rooms are small with no view, and fittings are dated in places; ask for a deluxe room on a higher floor.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Sonam Delek from MG Marg
faqs.a: It is a short walk, usually 5–10 minutes, along Tibet Road from the top end of MG Marg. Tibet Road has a gentle climb, so it is easy with day bags but tiring with large suitcases. Ask your driver to drop you at the door on arrival. Once settled, you will rarely need a taxi for the town centre, which saves money every evening.

faqs.q: Do rooms at Sonam Delek have a mountain view
faqs.a: The deluxe and super deluxe rooms on the upper floors face the Kangchenjunga range and many have balconies. Standard twins are cheaper and usually have no view. Views are clearest from October to early December and from February to April, mostly at sunrise. In the monsoon months cloud often hides the range for days, so the cheaper room makes more sense then.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Sonam Delek good for a budget Gangtok trip
faqs.a: Yes, if location matters more to you than polish. Standard rooms are among the cheaper options this close to MG Marg, roughly ₹1,800–2,500 off-season and more in peak weeks, indicative 2026. You walk to the promenade, markets and shared-taxi stands, which keeps daily spending low. Expect simple rooms and a basic breakfast. Remember Sikkim's ₹50 per tourist fee collected at check-in; check current status before you travel.

name: Mintokling Guest House
summary: A family-run guest house on Bhanu Path, off Secretariat Road, set in a small garden a short walk below the town centre. Rooms are spacious and quiet, the style is Sikkimese, and it suits travellers who want a calm base rather than a hotel on the main road.
body: Mintokling sits on Bhanu Path, a lane near the Secretariat, about half a kilometre from the centre of Gangtok. The house is built in a traditional Sikkimese style with painted wood and a garden in front, and it has a residential feel that the big MG Marg hotels lack. The lane is quiet after dark, which matters in a town where traffic hums until late on the main roads.

Rooms range from deluxe doubles and twins to a superior room and a suite, and they are larger than most budget rooms in town. There is parking, Wi-Fi and a 24-hour front desk. Reviews are mostly warm about space and cleanliness, with a few complaints about the walk and the service on busy days. Book direct or through the usual platforms, and confirm whether breakfast is included.
why: Quiet lane with a garden, away from main-road traffic
Bigger rooms than most budget hotels in Gangtok
Traditional Sikkimese house style
watch_out: The walk back up to MG Marg is steep for older travellers, so budget ₹100–150 for short taxi hops.

faqs.q: Where exactly is Mintokling Guest House in Gangtok
faqs.a: It is on Bhanu Path, off Secretariat Road, roughly 500–700 metres from the MG Marg area. Gangtok is built on a ridge, so the walk into town involves a climb. Fit walkers manage it in 10–15 minutes. Local shared taxis pass on the main road nearby and charge ₹20–40 a seat, indicative 2026, which is the easy way back after dinner.

faqs.q: Is Mintokling a homestay or a hotel
faqs.a: It sits in between. Mintokling is a family-run guest house in a traditional-style house with a garden, so it feels more personal than a hotel, but it has a front desk, parking and several room grades like a small hotel. It suits people who want quiet and space more than a lobby, lift and room service menu.

faqs.q: Is Mintokling good for families with older parents
faqs.a: The rooms are spacious and the lane is quiet, which suits families. The catch is the slope: walking up to MG Marg is tiring for older people, and there is no flat stroll from the door. If your parents are slow on hills, plan taxi rides into town for ₹100–150 each way and choose a ground-floor room if one is free.

name: Hotel Tibet
summary: An older, mid-sized hotel on Paljor Stadium Road with about thirty rooms decorated in Tibetan style, a short walk from MG Marg. It sits at the top of the budget band and is a safe pick for travellers who want a proper hotel with a restaurant at a fair price.
body: Hotel Tibet stands on Paljor Stadium Road, close to the stadium and within walking distance of MG Marg. It has around thirty rooms finished in a traditional Tibetan style, with painted woodwork and thangka-style art, plus a traditional hall used for meetings and dinners. The Sikkim government gave it a Best Hotel recognition in 2008, though that was a while ago and we judge it on what it is today: a dependable, slightly old-fashioned town hotel.

Rooms on the valley side get mountain views in clear weather. The restaurant is useful on cold evenings when you do not want to walk out for dinner. Rates stay moderate for the location, which is why we place it in our budget tier even though it feels more like a mid-range hotel. Book early for October and May, when Bengali and North Indian holiday crowds fill Gangtok.
why: Walkable to MG Marg and Paljor Stadium Road shops
Tibetan-style rooms with a real sense of place
In-house restaurant for cold or wet evenings
watch_out: Parts of the building and bathrooms show their age; ask for a renovated, valley-facing room.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Tibet from MG Marg
faqs.a: It is on Paljor Stadium Road, roughly a 5–10 minute walk from MG Marg depending on which end you head for. The road is busy with traffic, so take the footpath side. Being this close saves you taxi money in the evenings, and you can walk to the main markets, the ropeway and several cafes.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Tibet have a restaurant
faqs.a: Yes, the hotel has an in-house restaurant, and it also has a traditional-style hall used for group dinners and meetings. The restaurant is handy in winter and in the monsoon, when walking out at night is cold or wet. For cheaper local food, MG Marg and Lal Bazaar are a short walk away, where momos cost ₹60–150 a plate, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Tibet budget or mid-range
faqs.a: It sits at the top of the budget band. Indicative 2026 rates run about ₹3,000–5,500 per room night depending on season and room type. That is more than a basic lodge but less than most hotels with this location and an in-house restaurant. We list it as budget because it gives good value for families who want a proper hotel without paying mid-range prices.

name: Netuk House
summary: A family-owned heritage house on Tibet Road, built in the 1950s by a counsellor to the Chogyal on what was then the main road out of Gangtok towards Tibet. Rooms mix traditional and modern styles, and the kitchen cooks Sikkimese dishes with fern shoots and nettle.
body: Netuk House was built in the 1950s by an executive counsellor to the then Chogyal of Sikkim, on Tibet Road. At the time this road was the start of the trail that traders and travellers took north and east towards the passes into Tibet. The family, the Denzongpas, still own it. The house was built in the traditional way with local materials, and it reads as a home first and a hotel second.

You can choose between traditional and more modern rooms; some have balconies or sit-outs facing the Kangchenjunga range. The restaurant is the reason many guests come back: it serves Sikkimese home food, including dishes made with fiddlehead fern and stinging nettle, which are hard to find on Gangtok menus. There is a small bar and parking, and MG Marg is a short walk away.
why: Real 1950s Sikkimese house with a story tied to the Chogyal's court
Sikkimese home cooking with fern and nettle dishes
Short walk to MG Marg yet quieter than the main road
watch_out: Old-house layout means uneven floors, stairs and no lift, and rooms differ a lot, so ask for photos of the exact room.

faqs.q: What is the history of Netuk House in Gangtok
faqs.a: Netuk House was built in the 1950s on Tibet Road by an executive counsellor to the Chogyal, the king of Sikkim. Tibet Road was then the main route for travellers and traders heading north towards Tibet, and the house later served as a stop for traders. It is still owned by the same Sikkimese family and run as a small heritage stay.

faqs.q: Does Netuk House serve local Sikkimese food
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the best reason to stay. The kitchen cooks Sikkimese home-style dishes, including recipes with fiddlehead fern and stinging nettle that most Gangtok restaurants do not serve. Ask about dinner when you book so the kitchen can plan. If you are not staying there, ask whether outside guests can book a meal; policies change, so confirm first.

faqs.q: Is Netuk House suitable for elderly travellers
faqs.a: It works for active older travellers, but not for anyone who struggles with stairs. It is an old house, so there is no lift, floors can be uneven and rooms are spread over levels. Tell the hotel when booking and ask for a room with the fewest steps. Tibet Road itself is a gentle slope to MG Marg.

name: The Royal Plaza
summary: One of the larger hotels in Gangtok, in Upper Syari about 10 minutes by car from MG Marg. Around 78 rooms over five floors, a lift, meeting halls and the full kit of a conventional four-star. A sound family choice when you want space, parking and predictability.
body: The Royal Plaza is in Upper Syari, a residential area above the town centre. Built in 2004 and renovated since, it has around 78 rooms over five floors, lifts, parking and meeting rooms that host weddings and conferences. That size is useful for families and groups: rooms are bigger than in central Gangtok, and the hotel copes well with early departures for Tsomgo or North Sikkim.

The trade-off is distance. MG Marg is a 10-minute drive or a longer walk downhill and back up, so budget for taxis. Reviews are a mix: guests like the rooms and the setting; some mention slow room service and uneven food at busy times. For a quiet base with a lift and dependable hot water, it is a reasonable comfort-tier pick.
why: Large rooms and lifts suit families and older travellers
Parking and early-start friendly for Tsomgo and North Sikkim trips
Quieter residential area above the town
watch_out: It is not walkable to MG Marg for most people, so add ₹200–400 a day for local taxis.

faqs.q: How far is The Royal Plaza from MG Marg
faqs.a: The hotel is in Upper Syari, roughly 2–3 km by road from MG Marg, about 10 minutes by car outside rush hour. Walking down is possible, but the return climb is steep. Most guests use local taxis at ₹150–250 a trip, indicative 2026. If you plan to spend every evening on MG Marg, a central hotel may work out cheaper overall.

faqs.q: Is The Royal Plaza good for families
faqs.a: Yes. It is a large hotel with lifts, bigger rooms than most central Gangtok properties, parking for your vehicle and a restaurant on site. Those things matter with children or grandparents. It also handles 6 am departures for Tsomgo Lake and North Sikkim without fuss. The trade-off is that you need a taxi for the MG Marg evening stroll.

faqs.q: Does The Royal Plaza have a lift
faqs.a: Yes, the hotel has five floors served by lifts, which is not a given in Gangtok, where many older buildings rely on stairs down the hillside. This is one reason we suggest it for seniors and families with heavy luggage. Ask for a room facing the valley for views across to the mountains on clear mornings.

name: Bamboo Retreat
summary: A small, 12-room retreat in the hills below Rumtek, about 5 km from the monastery and roughly an hour from Gangtok. Gardens, a library, a meditation room and home-style meals make it a quiet alternative to staying in town, especially for monastery-focused trips.
body: Bamboo Retreat sits on a slope in the countryside around Rumtek, roughly 5–6 km from Rumtek Monastery and about an hour's drive from central Gangtok. It is small, with 12 rooms named after colours, and most have balconies over the valley. The common spaces are the draw: a library, a dining room hung with local artefacts and a meditation room.

The retreat also offers traditional hot-stone baths, cooking sessions and cultural activities, which you should book in advance and pay for separately. Food is home-style and served in the dining room. It is not a base for Gangtok nightlife or quick shopping trips, but for early mornings at Rumtek, walks to Old Rumtek and Ranka, and simply resting between long drives to the passes, it works well.
why: Close to Rumtek Monastery for prayer-hour visits
Quiet, small and set in gardens
Library, meditation room and hot-stone baths
watch_out: You need a car for almost everything, including Gangtok (about an hour), and evening options outside the retreat are close to nil.

faqs.q: How far is Bamboo Retreat from Rumtek Monastery
faqs.a: It is roughly 5–6 km from Rumtek Monastery, about 15–20 minutes by car on hill roads. That is close enough to reach the morning prayers or the golden stupa before day-trippers arrive from Gangtok. Arrange a car through the retreat or a Gangtok driver; there is no reliable walking route for most guests.

faqs.q: How far is Bamboo Retreat from Gangtok
faqs.a: Plan on about an hour by car from central Gangtok, depending on traffic at Ranipool and road works. A reserved car usually costs ₹1,500–2,500 one way, indicative 2026. It makes sense to stay here for two nights and do Rumtek, Old Rumtek and Ranka from the door, then move to Gangtok for Tsomgo Lake and MG Marg.

faqs.q: What activities does Bamboo Retreat offer
faqs.a: The retreat lists traditional hot-stone baths, cooking sessions and cultural activities, alongside a library and a meditation room that guests can use. Book activities ahead, as they depend on staff and season, and expect to pay extra for them. The rest is walking the lanes, reading and visiting the monasteries nearby.

name: Mayfair Spa Resort and Casino, Gangtok
summary: A large resort in Lower Samdur, off the Ranipool side of the highway below Gangtok, with a full spa, several restaurants and a casino. It is the comfortable, self-contained choice for couples and families who want to spend real time at the hotel, not just sleep there.
body: Mayfair sits in Lower Samdur, below the town on the Ranipool side, around 9 km and 25–30 minutes from MG Marg depending on traffic. The grounds are spread over a hillside with gardens, a spa, a swimming pool, multiple restaurants and a casino, so many guests stay on site for evenings and a slow morning between sightseeing days.

Rooms are large and well heated, which matters from December to February when Gangtok nights drop close to freezing. Being below the town also means you avoid some of the steepest central traffic on the way in from Siliguri. The cost is distance: every trip to MG Marg needs a car, and the hotel's prices for food and extras are what you would expect from a resort of this class.
why: Full spa, pool and several restaurants on site
Spacious, well-heated rooms for winter trips
Closer to the Siliguri highway for arrival and departure days
watch_out: It is about 9 km below MG Marg, so you depend on cars for town visits, and food and spa extras add up fast.

faqs.q: How far is Mayfair Gangtok from MG Marg
faqs.a: Mayfair is in Lower Samdur on the Ranipool side, roughly 9 km from MG Marg. Allow 25–30 minutes by car, longer in evening traffic. A one-way taxi typically costs ₹400–700, indicative 2026, and the hotel can arrange cars. If you want to stroll MG Marg every night, a central hotel fits better; Mayfair suits those happy to spend evenings on site.

faqs.q: Is Mayfair Gangtok good for a honeymoon
faqs.a: Many couples choose it because the resort has a spa, a pool, several restaurants and large heated rooms, so you can rest well between early starts for Tsomgo Lake or Nathu La. It feels separate from the town traffic. Keep in mind the 25–30 minute drive to MG Marg and the resort-level prices for meals and treatments.

faqs.q: Does Mayfair Gangtok have a casino
faqs.a: Yes, the resort operates a casino on site, which is legal in Sikkim under state law. Entry rules, age limits, dress codes and timings are set by the operator and can change, so ask at the front desk. Families who are not interested can ignore it; the casino is separate from the main rooms and spa areas.

name: The Elgin Nor-Khill
summary: A former royal guest house on Paljor Stadium Road, built in 1932 by the Chogyal of Sikkim to host state visitors. Today it is a heritage hotel with old photographs and antiques on the walls, gardens, a spa and a walkable location close to MG Marg.
body: Nor-Khill was built in 1932 by the ruling Chogyal of Sikkim as the state guest house, where visiting officials and guests of the palace stayed. It sits on Paljor Stadium Road, in walking distance of MG Marg, with lawns in front and the hill rising behind. The Elgin group now runs it, and it keeps the feel of an old official residence: oil paintings, archive photographs of the royal family and antique furniture in the corridors.

Rooms vary by wing and age; the older rooms carry the character, the newer ones more space and modern bathrooms. There is a spa and a restaurant serving Sikkimese and Indian food. We like it for travellers who want history in their stay and want to walk into town, rather than drive down from a resort.
why: 1932 royal guest house with genuine history on the walls
Walkable to MG Marg and Paljor Stadium Road
Gardens and a spa in the middle of town
watch_out: Heritage rooms differ in size and light, and the stadium side can be noisy during events, so ask for a garden-facing room.

faqs.q: What is the history of the Elgin Nor-Khill
faqs.a: It was built in 1932 by the Chogyal of Sikkim as the royal state guest house, where official visitors to the kingdom stayed. Sikkim was a separate kingdom until 1975. The building keeps that past on display through old photographs of the royal family, oil paintings and antique furniture. It is now run by the Elgin hotel group as a heritage hotel.

faqs.q: Can you walk from Elgin Nor-Khill to MG Marg
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel is on Paljor Stadium Road and most guests walk to MG Marg in 10–15 minutes. The route has some slope but is manageable for most adults. That walkability saves taxi costs and makes evening strolls easy, which is a real advantage over resorts several kilometres below the town.

faqs.q: Is Elgin Nor-Khill worth the price
faqs.a: It is if you value history and location. You pay a premium for a 1932 royal guest house in the centre of Gangtok, with gardens and a spa. Rooms vary, so ask for photos before you pay. If you mainly want a big modern room and resort facilities, Mayfair or Taj Guras Kutir may suit you better.

name: Taj Guras Kutir Resort and Spa
summary: IHCL's Taj resort above Gangtok, opened in September 2023 in the forested Pangthang area about 20 minutes from the city. Sixty-nine rooms and suites on 14 acres, with Kangchenjunga views, Sikkimese design touches and a spa. The top-end pick in East Sikkim right now.
body: Taj Guras Kutir opened in September 2023 in Pangthang, a forested ridge about 6 km and 20 minutes above Gangtok. Guras is the Nepali word for rhododendron, Sikkim's state tree. The resort has 69 rooms and suites spread across 14 acres, with views across to the Kangchenjunga range when the sky is clear, and a design that borrows from Sikkimese architecture and craft.

It is the quietest of the premium options: no traffic, cool forest air and a spa, which suits couples and anyone resting between long drives to Tsomgo, Nathu La or North Sikkim. Pangthang is also close to the edge of the Fambong Lho Wildlife Sanctuary. The drawback is cost and distance: every visit to MG Marg needs a car, and prices for meals reflect the brand.
why: Newest top-end resort near Gangtok, opened 2023
Forest setting with Kangchenjunga views on clear days
Spa and quiet grounds for rest days
watch_out: It is 20 minutes from town and rates are the highest in Gangtok, so you pay for cars and on-site dining on top.

faqs.q: Where is Taj Guras Kutir in Gangtok
faqs.a: It is in Pangthang, a forested area roughly 6 km above Gangtok, about a 20-minute drive from the city centre. The location is quiet and cool, with views to the Kangchenjunga range on clear days. You will need a car for MG Marg and sightseeing; the hotel can arrange one, or your tour vehicle can collect you.

faqs.q: When did Taj Guras Kutir open
faqs.a: IHCL, the Taj group's parent company, announced the opening in September 2023. It has 69 rooms and suites across about 14 acres. Because it is new, rooms and facilities are the most modern in the Gangtok area. Check current rates and offers directly with the hotel, as pricing changes a lot between peak and off-season months.

faqs.q: Is Taj Guras Kutir worth it over staying in town
faqs.a: Choose it if rest and views are the point of the trip, for example a honeymoon or a slower family holiday. You get quiet forest surroundings and a spa. If you want to walk MG Marg every evening and keep costs down, a central hotel is better value. Many couples split the stay: two nights in town, two at the resort.
